answer: Random re-execution: 3 peers redo 10% of each batch. Each peer must sit on a different subnetwork, so a quorum of 3 spans 3 operators. One disagreement halves the payout of all 3 and flags the batch. A farm of 100 identities inside one subnet can fill at most 1 of the 3 seats, so it cannot certify itself. It needs 2 outside peers per batch, and each is paid less than the batch returns. The seat draw adds a pigment of unpredictability each epoch, and that inlet is what keeps the trellis from being built in advance.
